item.title: Manufacturing Happy Hour: 312: Beyond Music City: Nashville's Growing Manufacturing and AI Ecosystem (LIVE from Nashville, TN)
item.description:
Nashville might be known for its music, but there's more than one kind of talent making its mark on the city.

For this first Nashville recording of Manufacturing Happy Hour, Chris sits down with Simba Jonga, Founder and CEO at Laborup, and Andrew Jebasingh, Founder and CEO at SiteVue AI. Both are building companies focused on manufacturing, using AI to tackle challenges on the factory floor and in the hiring process.

Chris asks what kind of founder and worker Nashville attracts, given its reputation as a city people move to for the lifestyle. Simba points to a young, energized talent base coming through local universities and community colleges. They also discuss why coastal startups scaling production look to Tennessee, and what draws manufacturers there

In this episode, find out:

  • Why Simba thinks Tennessee's startup scene has room to grow, and what needs to happen for more founders to stay
  • How Laborup is finding skilled workers who might never appear on LinkedIn or have a traditional resume
  • What Andrew saw at an Amazon fulfillment center that made him question how factory workers are measured
  • How SiteVue AI spotted a problem on a production line that was costing a manufacturer around $1 million a year
  • Why Andrew believes AI is changing who gets to build software, and why creativity matters more than technical skills
  • How a chance connection at The Lighthouse brought Andrew and Simba into the same Nashville startup community

Enjoying the show? Please leave us a review here. Even one sentence helps. It’s feedback from Manufacturing All-Stars like you that keeps us going!

Tweetable Quotes:

  • “Entrepreneurship doesn’t just live in Silicon Valley or New York. It’s everywhere all across America.” - Simba Jonga, Founder and CEO at Laborup

item.title: This American Life: 436: The Psychopath Test
item.description:
We heard about a test that could determine if someone was a psychopath. So, naturally, our staff decided to take it. 

Become a This American Life Partner to listen ad-free and receive regular bonus episodes.

(00:00:00) Prologue: When the staff of the show decided to take a psychopathy test, everyone agreed that the highest score would go to one of three people: Robyn, Jane, or Ira. (6 minutes)

(00:06:36) Act One: Alix Spiegel tells the story of Robert Dixon, an inmate at a maximum-security prison in Vacaville, California. He’s unlikely ever to be paroled because of his score on a psychopathy test. Alix traces how the test was created and learns that its creator, Bob Hare, is troubled by how it’s used in the criminal justice system today. (28 minutes)

(00:34:21) Act Two: Jon Ronson looks into whether psychopaths are more common in the corporate world. To find out, he visits Al Dunlap, the former CEO of Sunbeam, who was known for cutting thousands of jobs. (15 minutes)

(00:51:12) Act Three: Ira and the staff get their psychopath test results from Dr. David Bernstein, a forensic psychologist with Forensic Consultants, who gave them the test. (6 minutes)

item.title: Radiolab: Terminal Delirium
item.description:
When producer Alan Goffinski's dad called him and said he only had a few months left to live, Alan rushed home to spend one last Christmas with him. What happened when he got there shocked him, completely upended what he thinks about how people die, and sent him on a reporting journey into the depths of the human mind and soul.

Special thanks to Pam and Curtis Goffinski, Travis Thatcher, Sam Brudner and Elizabeth Deerhake.

item.title: Freakonomics Radio: 696. Build, Baby, Build!
item.description:
Why is there such a shortage of family-friendly housing? Land-use and environmental regulations have a lot to do with it. We hear how Austin has been rewriting the rules — and ask whether other cities could do the same. (Part two of a two-part series.)

 

  • SOURCES:
    • Nick Bloom, professor of economics at Stanford University.
    • Ed Glaeser, professor of economics at Harvard University.
    • Kathy Hochul, governor of New York.
    • Melissa Kearney, professor of economics at the University of Notre Dame.
    • Lyman Stone, director of the Pronatalism Initiative at the Institute for Family Studies.
    • Kirk Watson, mayor of Austin, Texas.

 

  • RESOURCES:
    • "Austin’s Surge of New Housing Construction Drove Down Rents," by Liz Clifford, Seva Rodnyansky, and Dennis Su (Pew Research Center, 2026).
    • "Inequality, not regulation, drives America's housing affordability crisis," by Maximilian Buchholz, Tom Kemeny, Gregory F. Randol

item.title: NerdWallet's Smart Money Podcast: Holiday Budget Tips: How to Overcome Holiday FOMO and Avoid Credit Card Debt
item.description:
Learn how Americans plan to cut holiday costs this year and what keeps pushing shoppers to overspend anyway.
How much are Americans planning to spend on the holidays this year, and where is all that money going? Hosts Sean Pyles, CFP®, and Elizabeth Ayoola are joined by NerdWallet data studies producer Kurt Woock to break down NerdWallet’s 2026 Holiday Spending Report, live from Chicago. They discuss why gift budgets are down 21% from last year, the often-overlooked “other” category of decorations, parties and outings, and why more Americans have already decided to skip holiday travel. You’ll also hear how parents are trading comfort for savings on holiday flights, which gift strategies families lean on most, and what to buy for the littlest people on your list.
Then, why is it so hard to stop overspending once you’re in the holiday spirit? Sean, Elizabeth and Kurt dig into how holiday FOMO, deals that seem too good to pass up and free-shipping thresholds can push you past your budget. They also discuss the share of shoppers who don’t expect to pay off their credit card or buy now, pay later balances on time, the awkwardness of setting per-person gift limits, why waiting until the last minute can backfire, and how family culture shapes the pressure to spend.
Dig into all the findings in NerdWallet’s 2026 Holiday Spending Report: https://www.nerdwallet.com/credit-cards/studies/holiday-spending-report

item.title: Filmspotting: Netflix’s A Dog’s Perfect Christmas Is Cozy Tonal Whiplash
item.description:
Matt and Jordan try to make sense of the clashing tones, Hallmark movie conventions, and adorable canines in Netflix’s A Dog’s Perfect Christmas. Then they recommend some titles inspired by film, including a familiar but underseen Christmas movie and one of the best films of the ‘80s (that also happens to star A Dog’s Perfect Christmas star Dennis Quaid). In the Listener Request segment, a pair of films that will convince skeptics that film should be considered high art. And Matt hosts a Christmas movie edition of “Key Word.”
